user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information, John. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need you to perform a quick check on your phone to confirm if it can currently send MMS messages.

Please use the diagnostic tool or setting on your phone to check if MMS sending is possible. If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know what type of phone you have (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.

Once you’ve checked, let me know the result, and we’ll proceed with the next troubleshooting steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I checked, and it looks like my phone can’t send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since your phone cannot send MMS messages, let’s start troubleshooting. First, I need to confirm that your phone has cellular service and mobile data, as both are required for MMS.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- Do you see any signal bars, or does it say “No Service”?
- Is mobile data (4G, 5G, LTE, etc.) showing as active?
- Is Airplane Mode turned off?

Let me know what you see, and we’ll continue from there.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see full signal bars with a little “5G” symbol, and it says data is enabled. Airplane mode isn’t on. What should I check next?

Great, that means your cellular service and mobile data are active, and Airplane Mode is off. Next, let’s check if your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings are correct, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed. If you’re not sure how to check this, let me know your phone model (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL listed. I’m not really sure what that means—does that explain why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do now?

Thank you for checking. Yes, not having an MMSC URL in your APN settings can definitely prevent you from sending or receiving MMS (picture messages).

To fix this, you should reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device? If so, please let me know if you’re using an Android or iPhone, and I’ll guide you through the process.

I’m not sure what kind of phone I have, but I get really nervous about changing settings and especially about rebooting. Will I lose any of my photos or messages if I reset the APN or restart my phone? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Rest assured, resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. These actions only affect your phone’s network connection settings and simply restart your device, similar to turning it off and back on.

Your personal content—such as photos, messages, contacts, and apps—will remain safe and unchanged.

Would you like me to guide you through the steps to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone? If you’re unsure about your phone type, I can provide general instructions or help you identify your device. Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. Do I need to restart my phone now? I’m still a bit anxious—can you reassure me again that nothing will disappear if I do this?

Yes, after resetting your APN settings, you do need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

I want to reassure you again: restarting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, contacts, or apps. It’s just like turning your phone off and then back on—your personal data will remain safe and unchanged.

Once you’ve restarted your phone, please try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works. If you have any concerns or need help with the restart, just let me know!

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...

Thank you for letting me know, and I understand how frustrating this can be. Let’s continue troubleshooting together—there are still a few more things we can check to get your MMS working.

Next, let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone, as this can sometimes interfere with sending MMS. Could you please check your phone’s settings and let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on? If it is, please try turning it off and then attempt to send a picture message again.

If you’re not sure how to check or turn off Wi-Fi Calling, let me know and I can guide you through the steps.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking that. Since Wi-Fi Calling is off, let’s check one more thing: your network mode. MMS requires at least a 3G connection, but you mentioned seeing “5G” earlier, which should be fine. However, let’s confirm your phone’s network mode preference to make sure it’s not set to an older mode like 2G or 3G only.

Could you please check your phone’s network mode settings and let me know what it’s set to? If you see options like “5G,” “4G,” or “LTE,” make sure one of those is selected (ideally “4G/5G preferred” or similar).

If you’re unsure how to check this, let me know and I can provide step-by-step instructions.
Network Mode Preference: 4g_5g_preferred
I checked my phone’s network mode, and it’s set to “4G/5G preferred.” Is that the right setting, or do I need to change anything else?

“4G/5G preferred” is the correct setting for MMS, so you don’t need to change anything there.

Let’s check one more possible cause: app permissions. Sometimes, the messaging app needs permission to access storage and SMS to send picture messages.

Could you check your messaging app’s permissions and confirm that it has access to both “storage” and “SMS”? If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know your phone type or if you need step-by-step instructions, and I’ll guide you through the process.
